snippet.title: How Much a Pirate's Head Was Actually Worth....
snippet.description: A hundred pounds. That was the figure a Virginia governor put on the head of the most feared man in the Atlantic world, and if you convert it honestly into what money means today, you land somewhere in the range of fifteen to twenty thousand pounds, which sounds like a lot until you remember this was the price for Edward Teach, the pirate the entire eastern seaboard called Blackbeard. Compare that to what an English sailor named Henry Every walked away with two decades earlier, something in the neighborhood of six hundred thousand pounds in stolen jewels and silver, a sum so staggering that converting it into modern terms gets you past a hundred million, and you start to see the strange arithmetic at the center of this story. The reward for catching the era's most notorious killer was a fraction of what a single successful pirate could steal on a good afternoon.
